2025.robotDescription: Calypso is CRyptonite's 25th competition robot, designed for the 2025 FIRST® Robotics Competition game, REEFSCAPE℠. In REEFSCAPE℠, teams are challenged to score Coral at multiple heights along the reef, process and score algae, and complete an endgame cage climb challenge. This robot features a swerve drive, three-stage elevator, a dual-purpose end effector, a ground intake, and deep climbing mechanism. Calypso is capable of delivering a four-piece all L4 autonomous route, as well as, scoring Coral at every level of the reef as well as scoring algae in both the barge and the processor. Advanced AprilTag vision enables fully automatic alignment to the reef. Throughout the season, Calypso helped CRyptonite earn multiple event finalist, the Excellence in Engineering Award, the Autonomous Award, and qualifications for the 2025 FIRST® World Championships.
robotFeatures: 114lbs without bumpers or battery
Swerve drive system
Three-stage elevator reaching 89 inches
Dual-purpose end effector
Ground intake with compliant wheels
Deep climbing mechanism

subsystems.title: End Effector
subsystems.description: The end effector is designed to pick up algae at level of the reef and score coral at all scoring levels. It is powered by Two Kraken x44, with one motor for pivot and the other one for the wheels.

subsystems.title: Ground Intake
subsystems.description: The ground intake is capable of picking up coral from any orientation using a combination of compliant star wheels, Versa rollers, and flex wheels. In addition to intake, this mechanism can score ground algae into the processor and score coral in L1. The intake is driven by a Kraken x60 for the rollers and a Kraken x44 for pivoting.

subsystems.title: Elevator
subsystems.description: The robot features a three stage continuous string elevator designed to reach all scoring levels as well as the barge. Powered by two Kraken x60 enabling fast stable vertical motion. The elevator has a starting height of 40 inches and extends to 89 inches.

subsystems.title: Drive Train
subsystems.description: This drivetrain is a 29 inch by 29 inch SDS MK4n L2+ Swerve Drive system. Each swerve module is powered by a Kraken x60 for drive and Kraken x44 for rotation.

subsystems.title: Feeder
subsystems.description: The feeder system uses compliant star wheels and flex wheels to center coral and position it consistently for hand off to the end effector. Driven by a single Kraken x44.

subsystems.title: Climber
subsystems.description: The climber is a two bar Deep Climb system that uses a hook latch mechanism. It is powered by a single Kraken x60 geared to a 197.53:1 reduction.

subsystems.title: Programming
subsystems.description: AprilTags vision is used to enable fully automatic scoring with Reef, Barge, and Human Player station. Preset position are implemented for Elevator, End Effector, Pivoting Intake, and Climb Mechanism. Autonomous paths are generated using PathPlanner and Choreo, and robot code is written in Java.

2024.robotDescription: Maestro is CRyptonite Robotics' 2024 competition robot, designed for the 2024 FIRST Robotics Competition game CRESCENDO. In this game, teams score foam rings known as Notes into the Amp and Speaker while completing an endgame climb. Maestro features a swerve drivetrain, an adjustable dual roller shooter, a fast under bumper intake, a pivoting shooter, and a two arm climbing mechanism capable of harmonizing. Maestro can score Notes from close and long distances and consistently score in the Amp. Advanced vision processing with AprilTags enables automatic shooter alignment, while object detection supports reliable Note intake. Throughout the season, Maestro contributed to multiple event wins and finalist finishes, the Engineering Inspiration Award, the Innovation in Control Award, and qualification for the 2024 FIRST World Championships. At Championships, Maestro led CRyptonite to Division Finalist, the furthest advancement in team history.

subsystems.description: Maestro’s swerve drive uses SDS MK4n modules providing fast acceleration, high maneuverability, and smooth motion control in a high collision game.

2023.robotDescription: Cassini is CRyptonite Robotics' 2023 competition robot, designed for the 2023 FIRST® Robotics Competition, Charged UP℠. In Charged UP℠, teams are challenged with scoring cones and cubes onto a three level grid and completing an endgame balance on the charge station. The robot features a swerve drivetrain, a pivoting three-stage telescoping elevator, and an end effector designed to hold both cubes and cones effectively. Advanced vision processing enables automatic alignment to the substation and scoring nodes, improving consistency during autonomous and teleoperated periods. Throughout the season, Cassini helped CRyptonite earn event wins, multiple Innovation in Control Awards, the Autonomous Award, and the qualification for the 2023 FIRST® World Championships

2022.robotDescription: Talos is CRyptonite Robotics’ 2022 competition robot, designed for the 2022 FIRST Robotics Competition game RAPID REACT. In this game, teams score cargo balls into the lower and upper hubs while completing a traversal climb during endgame. Talos features a swerve drivetrain, an over the bumper vector intake capable of holding two cargo balls, an adjustable hood shooter able to score in the upper hub, and a dual telescoping climbing mechanism capable of completing the highest traversal bar. Advanced vision processing enables accurate targeting and alignment for both autonomous and teleoperated scoring. Throughout the season, Talos contributed to multiple event wins and finalist finishes, the Innovation in Control Award, multiple Autonomous Awards, and the Excellence in Engineering Award at the FIRST World Championship. Talos finished the season ranked 1st in Texas, 7th in the United States, and 10th in the world in EPA, marking the highest ranking in team history.

2021.robotDescription: Deadshot is CRyptonite Robotics' 2020 and 2021 competition robot, designed for the FIRST Robotics Competition game INFINITE RECHARGE. In this game, teams shoot power cells into high and low goals and complete an endgame climb. The 2020 season was cut short due to Covid 19. Deadshot features a slap down intake, a turreted shooter, and a two arm endgame climb. Throughout the extended 2020 and 2021 season, Deadshot helped CRyptonite rank 3rd at The Texas Cup.

subsystems.title: Programming

2019.robotDescription: Impulse is CRyptonite Robotics’ 2019 competition robot, designed for the FIRST Robotics Competition game DEEP SPACE. In this game, teams placed hatch panels and cargo balls onto rockets and cargo ships while completing an endgame climb onto the HAB platform. Impulse is able to score both hatch panels and cargo balls at all levels of the rocket as well as in the cargo ship. It features a 3 stage elevator, a dual purpose end effector, and a tank drive. Throughout the season, Impulse helped CRyptonite earn multiple district and regional event wins, Innovation in Control Awards, the Autonomous Award, and qualification for the 2019 FIRST World Championships.

2018.robotDescription: PaCRat is CRyptonite Robotics’ 2018 competition robot designed for the FIRST Robotics Competition game FIRST POWER UP. In this game, teams score power cubes onto scales and switches, climb the tower during endgame, and work with alliance partners to control the field. PaCRat features a telescoping elevator capable of reaching all scoring positions, an end effector that doubles as an intake, a hook on the elevator for climbing, and deployable platforms for a buddy climb system. Throughout the season, PaCRat contributed to multiple regional wins, the Imagery Award, the Excellence in Engineering Award, and the Innovation in Control Award. PaCRat finished the season ranked 2nd in Texas, 8th in the United States, and 12th in the world in EPA.

2017.robotDescription: Nautilus is CRyptonite Robotics’ 2017 competition robot designed for the FIRST Robotics Competition game FIRST STEAMWORKS. In this game, teams score gears on rotors, launch balls into boilers, and climb ropes during endgame. Nautilus features a ground intake for game pieces, a spool climb mechanism for endgame, and a hood shooter. The robot is capable of scoring both gears and balls. Throughout the season, Nautilus contributed to a regional win, the Innovation in Control Award, the Safety Award, and the Chairman’s Award.

2016.robotDescription: Brimstone is CRyptonite Robotics’ 2016 competition robot designed for the FIRST Robotics Competition game FIRST STRONGHOLD. In this game, teams breach defenses, shoot boulders into towers, and scale the tower during endgame. Brimstone features a tank drive configuration optimized for rough terrain, a mechanical flap for manipulating defenses, a shooter for scoring boulders, and a climbing system. Throughout the season, Brimstone contributed to a regional finalist finish, the Industrial Safety Award, and the Innovation in Control Award.
